points.en: Cropping Intensity: The number of crops raised in a field during an agricultural year, calculated as (Gross Cropped Area / Net Sown Area) * 100.
points.hi: Cropping Intensity: The number of crops raised in a field during an agricultural year, calculated as (Gross Cropped Area / Net Sown Area) * 100.

points.en: Multiple Cropping: Growing two or more crops on the same land in one calendar year, vital for maximizing productivity in smallholder farming systems.
points.hi: Multiple Cropping: Growing two or more crops on the same land in one calendar year, vital for maximizing productivity in smallholder farming systems.

points.en: Intercropping: Growing two or more crops simultaneously in a definite pattern on the same field to optimize resource use and risk mitigation.
points.hi: Intercropping: Growing two or more crops simultaneously in a definite pattern on the same field to optimize resource use and risk mitigation.

points.en: Relay Cropping: Sowing a succeeding crop before the harvest of the standing crop, minimizing turnaround time between crop seasons.
points.hi: Relay Cropping: Sowing a succeeding crop before the harvest of the standing crop, minimizing turnaround time between crop seasons.

points.en: Monoculture: Growing the same crop year after year on the same land, leading to soil depletion and pest build-up.
points.hi: Monoculture: Growing the same crop year after year on the same land, leading to soil depletion and pest build-up.

points.en: Mixed Cropping: Growing two or more crops simultaneously without any distinct row arrangement, often used as an insurance against crop failure.
points.hi: Mixed Cropping: Growing two or more crops simultaneously without any distinct row arrangement, often used as an insurance against crop failure.

points.en: Ratooning: Using the crop stubble/regrowth after harvesting the primary crop to produce a second harvest (common in sugarcane and banana).
points.hi: Ratooning: Using the crop stubble/regrowth after harvesting the primary crop to produce a second harvest (common in sugarcane and banana).

points.en: Seqential Cropping: Growing two or more crops in sequence on the same field per year where the succeeding crop is planted after the preceding one is harvested.
points.hi: Seqential Cropping: Growing two or more crops in sequence on the same field per year where the succeeding crop is planted after the preceding one is harvested.

explanation.en: Helps recall the four primary intensification strategies used in Indian agriculture to boost productivity per unit area.
explanation.hi: Helps recall the four primary intensification strategies used in Indian agriculture to boost productivity per unit area.

answer.en: It measures the number of times a field is cropped in a given agricultural year, expressed as a percentage of Net Sown Area.

question.en: How does Intercropping differ from Mixed Cropping?
question.hi: How does Intercropping differ from Mixed Cropping?

answer.en: Intercropping involves a definite row arrangement and complementary interaction, whereas mixed cropping involves sowing seeds mixed together without row patterns.
answer.hi: Intercropping involves a definite row arrangement and complementary interaction, whereas mixed cropping involves sowing seeds mixed together without row patterns.

misconception.en: Gross Cropped Area and Net Sown Area are the same thing.
misconception.hi: Gross Cropped Area and Net Sown Area are the same thing.

correction.en: Net Sown Area is the actual physical land area sown once, while Gross Cropped Area includes area sown multiple times in a year.
correction.hi: Net Sown Area is the actual physical land area sown once, while Gross Cropped Area includes area sown multiple times in a year.

fiveFacts.en: High cropping intensity reflects better irrigation coverage and short-duration crop varieties.
fiveFacts.hi: High cropping intensity reflects better irrigation coverage and short-duration crop varieties.

fiveFacts.en: Relay cropping eliminates the unproductive fallow period between harvests.
fiveFacts.hi: Relay cropping eliminates the unproductive fallow period between harvests.

fiveFacts.en: Monoculture drastically increases susceptibility to specific pests and soil exhaustion.
fiveFacts.hi: Monoculture drastically increases susceptibility to specific pests and soil exhaustion.

fiveFacts.en: Ratooning reduces cultivation costs but often results in declining yield over successive ratoons.
fiveFacts.hi: Ratooning reduces cultivation costs but often results in declining yield over successive ratoons.

fiveFacts.en: Intercropping improves nitrogen economy when a legume is paired with a cereal.
fiveFacts.hi: Intercropping improves nitrogen economy when a legume is paired with a cereal.
